battle.name: 夏威夷統一戰爭
battle.brief: 夏威夷統一戰爭歷時近二十年，1810年4月以瓦胡島上的一場和議收官：考艾島首領卡烏馬利伊答應效忠卡梅哈梅哈一世，考艾與尼伊哈烏自此併入王國。此前用來攻島的八百艘雙體戰舟與大批火槍重砲已集結待用，頭目們手中的燧發手槍，正是本卡輪發手槍點火原理的後裔。

kit.name: 輪發手槍
kit.history: 最早的後膛手槍。機械太貴，只給火槍隊的軍官與近衛。

countries: 夏威夷統一戰爭本質上是各島 mōʻī（首領）聯盟之間的兼併戰，而不是國家之間的戰爭。卡梅哈梅哈一世一方是科哈拉、科納與哈納三區的 aliʻi nui 聯合體：科哈拉的首領基納烏是他的同父異母兄弟兼首席謀臣，科納的卡阿胡馬努是他的政治搭檔與眾妻之一，凱庫豪皮奧是教他刀法與戰陣的老將，卡梅埃亞莫庫與卡馬納瓦是雙生叔父，基姆巴洛、凱阿卡烏、卡帕瓦各領一支部眾；宗教權力握在叔父卡拉尼奧普烏手中，他後來成為第一位 kahuna pule。戰士由各個 ahupuaʻa（土地單位）按慣例供應，臨時結集，裝備藤編的 pūloʻi 圓盾、標槍與短柄棍。對面則是各自獨立的島嶼王權：歐胡島的卡拉尼庫普萊、毛伊島的卡赫基利二世、考艾島的卡歐科庫拉尼與其子卡烏馬利伊，以及夏威夷島上仍在抵抗的科哈拉女首領豪努伊·卡韋納與希洛的納馬凱哈。1795年之後，卡梅哈梅哈把毛伊、莫洛凱、拉奈與歐胡的 mōʻī 逐一收編，戰爭的「交戰方」因此年年改寫成卡梅哈梅哈聯盟對一個聯盟殘餘的較量。
countriesEn: The Hawaiian unification wars were in truth wars of annexation between alliances of island mōʻī (chiefs), not wars between states. Kamehameha I's side was a coalition of the aliʻi nui of the districts of Kohala, Kona and Hāna: Kīnaʻu, his half-brother, chief of Kohala and senior counseller; Kaʻahumanu, his political partner and one of his many wives, of the Kona line; Kekūhaupiʻo, the old warrior who taught him swordwork and battle order; the twin uncles Kameʻeiamoku and Kamanawa; and Kīmballo, Keakaʻu and Kapawa, each commanding a body of retainers. Religious authority lay with his uncle Kalaniʻōpuʻu, who later became the first kahuna pule. Warriors were supplied by each ahupuaʻa (land division) as a matter of custom, mustered on demand, and armed with wicker pūloʻi round shields, javelins and short clubs. On the other side stood independent island sovereignties: Kalanikūpule of Oʻahu, Kahekili II of Maui, Kāʻeokūlani of Kauaʻi and his son Kaumualiʻi, together with Haʻunui Kāwena, the Kohala chiefess who still resisted, and Nāmakehā at Hilo. After 1795 Kamehameha absorbed the mōʻī of Maui, Molokaʻi, Lānaʻi and Oʻahu one by one, so that the opposing side year by year became a rump coalition facing Kamehameha's alliance.
people: 卡梅哈梅哈一世（約1736年或1758年生，1819年5月8日或14日卒）自幼由叔父卡拉尼奧普烏撫養，1782年叔父死後，他以舉起納哈石（Naha Stone）、實現「Ka Poukahi」預言的名聲登上歷史舞台，先在夏威夷島擊敗基瓦拉奧與科哈拉諸勢力。1795年他率960艘戰舟與約一萬名士兵登陸歐胡島。謀臣基納烏主張把歐胡守軍趕下努烏阿努峭壁，另一名 aliʻi 卡伊阿納卻倒向卡拉尼庫普萊，替對方在峭壁上的城砦鑿出炮口；卡梅哈梅哈遂派兩隊精兵攀上峭壁從背後奪炮，扭轉戰局。毛伊島的卡赫基利二世與其兄弟卡歐科庫拉尼曾聯手反攻，1791年在瓦皮奧外海的 Kepuwahaʻulaʻula 海戰中敗北；希洛的納馬凱哈叛亂則拖住卡梅哈梅哈整整六年。考艾島的凱歐烏阿·庫阿胡烏拉在普烏科霍拉海基亞落成後赴會，被卡梅哈梅哈的將領以長矛與火槍擊倒，島上的抵抗才告瓦解。1810年4月決定考艾命運的是王室系譜師兼大祭司卡拉伊庫阿胡盧：他主張留下卡烏馬利伊的性命、讓考艾成為朝貢之邦，化解了 aliʻi 議會毒殺的陰謀；另有兩個歐洲人——英國水手約翰·揚與美國人艾薩克·戴維斯，後者為卡烏馬利伊通風報信，卻被 aliʻi 毒殺；當時的夏威夷史家卡馬卡烏，正是靠他們與傳教士的記錄留下這場戰爭的細節。
peopleEn: Kamehameha I (born c. 1736 or 1758, died 8 or 14 May 1819) was raised by his uncle Kalaniʻōpuʻu and entered history in 1782, when the death of that uncle set the succession on Hawaiʻi Island between Kīwalaʻō and himself; the prophecy of Ka Poukahi and the lifting of the Naha Stone turned a dynastic quarrel into a contest of destiny. He took Kohala, Kona and Hāna on his own island first, and in 1795 crossed to Oʻahu with 960 war canoes and some ten thousand warriors. His counseller Kīnaʻu urged that the Oʻahu defenders be driven over the Nuʻuanu Pali, but the aliʻi Kaʻiana went over to Kalanikūpule and cut gun embrasures in the ridge for the fort's cannon; Kamehameha then sent two picked divisions up the cliff to seize the guns from behind, which turned the action. Kahekili II of Maui and his brother Kāʻeokūlani of Kauaʻi counter-attacked and were beaten in the naval battle of Kepuwahaʻulaʻula off Waipiʻo in 1791, while the revolt of Nāmakehā at Hilo kept Kamehameha busy for six long years. Keōua Kūʻahuʻula of Kaʻū and Puna was killed after the completion of the Puʻukoholā heiau in 1791, when he came to meet Kamehameha and was cut down by spear and musket fire, and with him the resistance on the island collapsed. In April 1810 the fate of Kauaʻi was settled by Kalaikuʻahulu, the royal genealogist and high priest, who argued for sparing Kaumualiʻi and making him a tributary ruler, thereby defeating the council's plan to poison the king; two Europeans also mattered, the British sailor John Young and the American Isaac Davis, the latter warning Kaumualiʻi of the plot and being poisoned by the aliʻi in his place. The Hawaiian historian Kamakau, and the missionaries who wrote down what they were told, are the reason the detail of these campaigns survives at all.
kits: 本卡的兵器是輪發手槍（Wheellock pistol），是16世紀初開始出現的自點火手槍：靠發條上弦，扳機帶動擊錘，齒輪摩擦擊出火星點燃火藥盤上的引火藥——主藥仍然由槍口裝入，改變嘅係點火方式而唔係裝藥方式。機件複雜、造價高昂，所以只配給火槍隊的軍官與近衛使用，尋常士兵仍用火繩長槍。必須老老實實說明：1810年的夏威夷沒有人手裡拿著輪發手槍，歐洲的輪發機制在17世紀已被燧發槍取代，島上真正流通的是滑膛燧發手槍與燧發火槍，它們隨商船貿易大量流入。戰場上最具決定性的其實是火炮：1790年「正義號」（Fair American）與「艾萊歐諾拉」（Eleanora）兩條船的貨艙裡有卡梅哈梅哈用來奪取毛伊島的火炮，1795年歐胡島一役則有從後方登陸奇襲而奪得的城砦重砲，砲位失守直接改變了攻守。島上原有的裝備則是傳統系統：藤編 pūloʻi 圓盾（一人高的圓形柳條盾，密排時可成盾牆）、短柄棍（ʻupʻupuaʻu）、標槍（ʻihe）、用作信號的螺殼號角（pūʻōlō），以及張著 kapa 樹皮布帆的雙體戰舟（peleleu）與單體戰舟（koa ʻia）。頭盔與披風是最昂貴的裝備：由夏威夷特有鳥類羽毛手工縫製的 mahiole 頭盔與 ʻahuʻula 披風只配首領佩戴，成為階級與戰意的標誌。
kitsEn: The card's weapon is the wheellock pistol, the self-igniting handgun that appeared at the opening of the sixteenth century: a spring wound on a drum, a sear and hammer that struck sparks, and a toothed wheel that ground against the frizzen to light the priming powder in the pan — the main charge was still loaded from the muzzle, so what the wheel-lock changed was the way of firing, not the way of loading, and it should not be mistaken for a breech-loading arm. The mechanism was too complex and too costly to issue to anyone but the officers and guards of the musketeers, so that common soldiers kept matchlock muskets. It must be said plainly that nobody in 1810 Hawaiʻi carried a wheellock: the wheel mechanism was superseded by the flintlock in the seventeenth century, and what circulated on the islands was the smoothbore flintlock pistol and flintlock musket, arriving in quantity through the trading ships. What decided the fighting was artillery: the holds of the Fair American and the Eleanora in 1790 yielded Kamehameha the cannon he used on Maui, and the 1795 fighting on Oʻahu turned on a heavy gun taken by surprise from the rear, the loss of its emplacement changing the whole course of the attack and defence. The indigenous equipment system was as follows: wicker pūloʻi round shields, woven willow hoops faced with planking, tall enough to be overlapped into a shield wall; short clubs (ʻupʻupuaʻu); the javelin (ʻihe); shell trumpets (pūʻōlō) for signals; and the double-hulled war canoe (peleleu) and single-hulled war canoe (koa ʻia) with sails of kapa barkcloth. The most expensive items were helmets and cloaks: the mahiole helmet and the ʻahuʻula cloak, hand-sewn from the feathers of Hawaiian birds, were worn by chiefs alone and served as the badge of rank and of fighting spirit.
tactics: 卡梅哈梅哈的戰術核心是「海陸同時、攻其必救」：1795年他以960艘戰舟同時掩護陸軍在歐胡島西岸的 Waiʻalae 與 Waiʻkīkī 兩處登陸，把守軍往東節節壓縮，最後趕上努烏阿努的帕里（Pali）峭壁。守方在峭壁頂用卡伊阿納鑿出的炮口架設重砲，卡梅哈梅哈的正面進攻受挫，於是抽出兩隊最精銳的戰士攀崖從背後奪炮，砲失而軍心潰散，聯軍乘勢以傳統長矛、標槍、火槍與火砲合擊，包圍成合圍之牆，壓垮對手。另一個關鍵是「齊射一輪再衝鋒」的戰法：先以火槍與旋轉小炮（swivel gun）齊射，再以棍矛衝鋒，把火力的短暫優勢轉成肉搏優勢，傳統記載把這套程序說成卡梅哈梅哈每日必下的號令，但細節諸說並存。1796年攻考艾島的失敗也說明其戰術的極限：艦隊在「Kaʻieʻie Waho」海峽遇大風浪，戰舟與載員大量損失，1804年再攻時又遇上「maʻi ʻokuʻu」疫病，軍隊大半被殘，計畫一延再延。到1810年，戰爭的最後一步反而不是攻城：雙方在瓦胡島談判，由卡烏馬利伊以朝貢換取留任，考艾與尼伊哈烏併入王國，十八年的戰事以一紙協議收場。
tacticsEn: The core of Kamehameha's method was to move by sea and land together and strike where the enemy must respond. In 1795 he used 960 war canoes to cover landings at Waiʻalae and Waikīkī on the west shore of Oʻahu, driving the defenders east until they were pinned against the Nuʻuanu Pali. The defenders had mounted heavy guns in embrasures cut by Kaʻiana along the ridge; Kamehameha's frontal attack stalled under that fire, and he detached two divisions of his best warriors to climb the cliff and take the guns from behind, and the loss of them broke the defenders' formation, so that the coalition pressed with spear, javelin, musket and cannon in an enclosing wall that crushed them. The other key was the drill of firing one volley and then charging: a volley of muskets and swivel guns first, and then a rush with clubs and spears, converting a fleeting advantage of firepower into an advantage at close quarters; the Hawaiian tradition makes this a standing order of Kamehameha's army, though the details vary from source to source. The failures of 1796 and 1804 mark the limits of the method: in the Kaʻieʻie Waho channel the fleet met heavy wind and sea and lost canoes and men in quantity, and the renewed attempt of 1804 was broken by the maʻi ʻokuʻu epidemic, which cut the army down and forced the plan to be deferred. By 1810 the last step of the war was not an assault at all: the parties negotiated on Oʻahu, and Kaumualiʻi exchanged submission for retention of his rule, Kauaʻi and Niʻihau joining the kingdom, so that eighteen years of war ended in an agreement rather than a breach.
data: 可查證的數字集中在兵力與船數上：1795年進攻歐胡島時，卡梅哈梅哈投入的艦隊為960艘戰舟，部隊約一萬人；同年夏天的努烏阿努之戰中，約七百人被逼從帕里峭壁（落差約一千英尺）墜下；希洛方面依卡馬卡烏的說法，建造了約八百艘雙體戰舟（peleleu）並大量屯積火槍、火炮與彈藥，1802至1803年間駐在毛伊，1803年底或1804年初移駐歐胡。1790年毛伊島的凱帕尼威之戰同樣靠商船得來的火炮取勝，1791年瓦皮奧外海的海戰則讓毛伊聯軍的艦隊全滅。人口與後果方面：1778年接觸前夏威夷人口約十二萬八千，1853年普查約七萬一千，1920年降至約二萬四千，但這主要是外來疫病造成，並非戰爭造成的傷亡。卡梅哈梅哈於1819年5月8日或14日去世，遺下數萬戰士與大量戰艦，1824年考艾島的胡梅胡梅叛亂仍靠這批軍力平定。關於本卡兵器的年份，只宜說明輪發手槍在1500年前後已出現並定型，1810年島上流通的是燧發手槍，兩者是原型與後裔的關係，並非同一件武器。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked are those of men and canoes. For the attack on Oʻahu in 1795 Kamehameha committed a fleet of 960 war canoes and a force of about ten thousand; in the fighting at Nuʻuanu in the summer of 1795 some seven hundred men were driven over the Pali, a drop of roughly a thousand feet. At Hilo, according to Kamakau, a fleet of about eight hundred double-hulled war canoes, the peleleu, was built and large quantities of muskets, cannon and ammunition were stockpiled; the court stayed on Maui from 1802 to 1803 and moved to Oʻahu in late 1803 or early 1804. The 1790 battle of Kepaniwai on Maui was likewise won with cannon taken from trading ships, and the 1791 action off Waipiʻo destroyed the Maui coalition fleet. On population and its aftermath: before contact in 1778 Hawaiʻi had roughly 128,000 people, the census of 1853 counted about 71,000, and the figure fell to some 24,000 by 1920, but this was caused chiefly by imported disease and not by the casualties of war. Kamehameha died on 8 or 14 May 1819 leaving tens of thousands of warriors and many warships, and the army he left was still what put down Humehume's rebellion on Kauaʻi in 1824. As for the card's weapon, the only safe statement is that the wheellock pistol had appeared and been standardised around 1500; the pistols actually circulating in Hawaiʻi in 1810 were flintlocks, and the relation between them is prototype and descendant, not identity.
cause: 戰爭的起因是夏威夷傳統政治結構本身容不下一個群島王國。傳統上每個島由一位 aliʻi nui 統治，島與島之間沒有常設的中央權力，也沒有任何可以跨海作戰的常備軍，卡梅哈梅哈要統一群島，等於要憑一島的資源去攻取另外五島。1782年叔父卡拉尼奧普烏去世後，夏威夷島的繼承在基瓦拉奧與卡梅哈梅哈之間裂開，「Ka Poukahi」預言與舉起納哈石的儀式把王位爭奪變成天命之爭；卡梅哈梅哈先取科哈拉、科納與哈納，1791年普烏科霍拉海基亞落成後再除掉凱歐烏阿·庫阿胡烏拉，接著把矛頭指向毛伊與歐胡的卡赫基利王朝。外部因素同樣關鍵：西方毛皮貿易帶來火槍、火炮與數量可觀的火藥，檀香木出口中國又把夏威夷人的戰爭經濟接上全球市場，甲板上的士兵第一次比傳統棍矛更值錢。1794年歐胡與毛伊之間的內鬥，以及卡拉尼庫普萊殺死叔父卡歐科庫拉尼所引起的考艾繼承危機，則令敵我界線在1795到1800年間反覆重畫。
causeEn: The war began because the traditional Hawaiian political order could not accommodate a single kingdom of the archipelago. Each island was ruled by its own aliʻi nui; there was no permanent central authority between the islands and no standing force capable of crossing the sea between them, so for Kamehameha to unite the archipelago meant taking six islands with the resources of one. When Kalaniʻōpuʻu died in 1782 the succession on Hawaiʻi Island split between Kīwalaʻō and Kamehameha, and the prophecy of Ka Poukahi together with the lifting of the Naha Stone turned that succession quarrel into a contest of fate. Kamehameha took Kohala, Kona and Hāna first, removed Keōua Kūʻahuʻula after the completion of the Puʻukoholā heiau in 1791, and then turned on the dynasty of Kahekili over Maui and Oʻahu. Outside factors mattered just as much: the western fur trade brought muskets, cannon and gunpowder in quantity, while the export of sandalwood to China tied the Native Hawaiian war economy into the world market, and for the first time a fighting man on a canoe deck was worth more than a man with a club. The civil war between Oʻahu and Maui in 1794, and the Kauaʻi succession crisis caused by Kalanikūpule's killing of his uncle Kāʻeokūlani, redrew the lines of the war again and again between 1795 and 1800.
impact: 統一之後，波利尼西亞出現了第一個以歐洲式君主制為框架的國家：卡梅哈梅哈把各島法律統一，廢除島際壁壘式的舊習慣，用《折斷的船槳法》（讓老弱婦孺在路邊安全休息）標誌新王權的道德主張；其妻卡阿胡馬努在他死後以 kahuʻāpuni 主持廢除 kapu 禁忌制度，接著1840與1852年的憲法、1848年的偉大分田（Great Māhele）把土地與稅制現代化，使夏威夷在1893年廢王與1959年建州之間的另一段歷史有了制度前提。文化上，卡梅哈梅哈的名字成為夏威夷國族象徵，1871年被定為公眾假期，其傳記由傳教士口述與《酋長傳說》等書寫整理，今日仍流通。人口上，島嶼在接觸後因外來疫病大幅下降，這是傳染病的後果而非戰爭的傷亡，卻重塑了整個社會結構；軍隊方面則誕生了太平洋第一支使用西式火砲、燧發槍與分級制度的海陸軍，1824年考艾島的胡梅胡梅叛亂即由這支軍隊平定。
impactEn: After the unification Polynesia had its first state built on the European monarchical model: Kamehameha unified the law of the islands, laid aside the old habit of inter-island barriers, and used the Law of the Splintered Paddle — that every old person, woman and child should lie by the roadside in safety — to proclaim the moral claim of the new kingship. His wife Kaʻahumanu, as kahuʻāpuni, abolished the kapu restrictions after his death; the constitutions of 1840 and 1852 and the Great Māhele of 1848 then modernised land and taxation, and gave the history that runs from the abolition of the monarchy in 1893 to statehood in 1959 its institutional premises. In cultural terms Kamehameha's name became the national symbol of Hawaiʻi, was made a public holiday in 1871, and his biography was written down from the accounts of the missionaries and the chiefs themselves, and still circulates today. Demographically, the islands' population fell steeply after contact because of imported disease — the consequence of contagion, not of the fighting — which reshaped the social order entirely. Militarily, the islands acquired the first Pacific navy and army to use Western artillery, flintlock muskets and a Western rank system, and it was that force which suppressed Humehume's rebellion on Kauaʻi in 1824.
result: 結果是彼此分離的島嶼王國從此消失。1795年的歐胡之役以帕里峭壁的血戰收尾：卡拉尼庫普萊被擒並獻祭給戰神庫卡伊利莫庫，歐胡與毛伊的 mōʻī 權力被逐一收編；1796年與1804年兩度攻取考艾島先後因海峽風浪與 maʻi ʻokuʻu 疫病而告吹，說明卡梅哈梅哈並非戰無不勝。真正完成統一的是政治手段：1810年4月，卡烏馬利伊在瓦胡島與卡梅哈梅哈達成協議，接受卡梅哈梅哈的宗主地位，保留考艾島的統治權，尼伊哈烏同時併入，考艾群島自此成為王國的一部分，十八年的兼併戰畫上句號。代價與收穫同樣清楚：戰爭把群島變成一個國家，也把檀香木貿易的利潤、歐洲火器與傳教士一起帶進來；aliʻi 議會原打算毒殺卡烏馬利伊、卻毒死了替他通風報信的艾薩克·戴維斯，是這場戰爭留下的最尖銳註腳——以火砲征服島嶼，最後靠一紙條款收編整座島。
resultEn: The result was the end of the separate island kingdoms. The Oʻahu campaign of 1795 ended in the fighting at the Pali: Kalanikūpule was taken and sacrificed to the war god Kūkāʻilimoku, and the mōʻī rights of Oʻahu and Maui were absorbed one by one. The two earlier attempts on Kauaʻi, in 1796 and 1804, failed through storm in the channel and through the maʻi ʻokuʻu epidemic, which is a reminder that Kamehameha was not invincible. What finally completed the unification was political: in April 1810 Kaumualiʻi came to terms with Kamehameha on Oʻahu, accepted his overlordship and kept his rule over Kauaʻi, while Niʻihau joined at the same time, and the island kingdom of Kauaʻi became part of the kingdom, closing eighteen years of annexation. The gains and the costs are both plain: the war turned an archipelago into a country, and at the same time opened the islands to the profits of the sandalwood trade, to European weapons and to missionaries; and the sharpest epigram left by the whole business is that the aliʻi council, having resolved to poison Kaumualiʻi, poisoned Isaac Davis instead — the man who had warned him. Islands were taken with cannon; a single clause of agreement took the island.
